newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, but prospects bright.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, but prospects bright.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.33 percent on Monday but traders said sentiment remains buoyant due to the strong performance of drug maker Lek's new shares.
Since being listed on September 11, Lek's new issue has risen 20.2 percent. Traders cited strong interest from foreign investors, which could help prop up the market for the next couple of weeks.
* The SBI index fell 3.05 percent to 915.81.
* Six shares fell and 11 rose, while seven were untraded.
* Turnover rose to 232.4 million tolars from 124.2 million on Friday.
* The A issue of Lek represented more than 75 percent of turnover, rising 3.4 percent to 16,550 on volume of 10,947 shares for total turnover of 177.4 million tolars.
* Bank UBK was the leading decliner, falling 9.89 percent to 7,350 on volume of one share.

* Ordinary shares of bank Hipotekarna banka Brezice were the top gainer, rising 6.67 percent to 3,400 on volume of three shares for total turnover of 0.01 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
